subject: phoenix
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: phoenix with flame plumage, wings spread.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a TypeScript module for a phoenix creature with flame plumage and spread wings, aiming for a Genshin Impact-inspired pyro aesthetic with gold trim and red-orange-teal accents, standing in a rest pose with wings extended.

I'm sketching the skeleton structure now — a hip root with a spine chain curving up through the chest to the neck and head, plus a trailing tail chain, sized for roughly 1.4m standing height and a 3.2m wingspan.

Still writing body sweep...

For the head, I'm designing a skull sphere with separate upper and lower beak spikes in gold-orange, connected via a jaw joint, with the head positioned at the neck's end and offset slightly forward. I'm adding flame-like crest plumes sweeping back from the crown with tapered gradients, plus stylized eyes with glowing teal or gold irises against white/gold sclera, dark pupils, Genshin-style.

For the wings, I'm building a chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist to hand tip, spreading outward and slightly upward with curved paths on each side, naming each joint per side for left/right symmetry. I'm planning flight feathers—primaries fanning from the wrist and secondaries along the forearm—styled like flame feathers to match the phoenix aesthetic.

Writing feather outlines...

Working out the orthogonal axis system...

Now I'm thinking through the color palette for the flame-feather gradient, aiming for a Genshin-style Pyro look: a gold base near the root transitioning through orange to a deep crimson at the tips, mapped along the outline's length coordinate for the paint callback.

Nesting gradients this way should work fine, and checking the texel budget, 100 feathers at that density stays well within the sheet's resolution limits, so the per-feather gradient approach is feasible.

I'm sketching a feather helper that takes base position, direction, length, width, bone data, and colors, then planning the wing structure: shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand-tip points define the arm, with secondaries fanning backward from the elbow-wrist segment and primaries fanning outward from the wrist toward the hand tip at increasing lengths to build the full wingspan.

Working through the arm proportions and primary feather lengths, I'm realizing the span comes out larger than a realistic bird but acceptable for a fantasy phoenix, so I'm trimming primary lengths slightly to keep the span closer to 4.6m. I'm also defining how primary feather angles fan from a forward-leaning angle to a backward angle along the hand axis, mirrored for left and right wings.

Now I'm laying out the feather distribution: primaries along wrist-to-handtip with angles shifting from near-outward at the tip to more backward near the wrist, secondaries along elbow-to-wrist with backward-leaning angles and shorter lengths, and tertials along shoulder-to-elbow, plus shorter covert feathers layered for visual depth.

I'm offsetting covert layers slightly upward in y to avoid z-fighting, and adding a gentle upward droop to the arm and outer feather tips so the wings form a soft V shape. I'm also considering an asymmetric feather outline with a straighter leading edge and a curved trailing edge for a more natural shape.

Defining feather outline points...

I could add a flame-like notch to the tip for extra visual interest, but I'll mark those notch corners as sharp so the smoothing algorithm doesn't throw errors on concave geometry — that keeps the cut edges safe for the unsharp corners nearby. Now let me actually define the flame shape.

For body plumage, I'm layering flat-filled flame shapes (red outer, orange middle, gold inner) as a texture scattered across the chest using cards, leaning back and down to follow the body's natural feather flow.

For the tail, I'm planning seven long ribbon-like feathers that sweep along curved catmull paths, trailing on the ground with S-curves, using a thin elliptical cross-section and a gold-to-orange-to-red gradient running from root to tip.

Still working out ribbon orientation and tapering width...

Now I'm sketching the tail bone chain extending back from the hips through a few segments.

Feathers will attach to the tail joints, fanning out from near the last segment with varying spread and length—longer at the center, shorter toward the sides—to create a trailing plume effect.

I'm plotting each feather path arcing from the rump down toward the floor so they lie gracefully behind the standing bird, keeping the lowest points just barely above the ground and giving the center feathers the longest reach.

Now I'm curling the tail tips upward slightly for a flame-like S-shape, and considering whether to scatter a few small floating ember shapes around the base for extra visual flair.

For the legs, I'm placing the hip joint and foot target, then building a three-segment digitigrade limb (thigh, tibia, tarsus) with lengths totaling more than the hip height so it comfortably reaches the ground, bending the knee forward and ankle back like a real bird.

Thickness tapers from thigh to ankle, colored with a gold scale paint for the leg surface. For the foot I'm planning three forward toes plus a back talon, built as simple rods extending from the foot joint.

I'm adding dark talon spikes at each toe tip, angling them slightly downward so they stay just above the ground plane. For the toes themselves, I'm structuring each as a single-joint chain parented to the foot joint, naming them like toeL1 and sweeping them as simple digit spans.

With four toes on each of two feet, that's eight chains total, each parented to the last joint in the leg chain and swept with a tapering radius and rounded caps. Now I'm moving on to the neck and head details, aiming for an elegant phoenix-like crest and flowing plumes reminiscent of Genshin's vermillion bird design.

For the head itself, I'm shaping a scaled sphere with a small curved beak in gold/amber, and for the eyes I'm planning a decal approach — an SVG-drawn anime-style eye with dark outline, gold iris, black pupil, and white highlights to capture that stylized look, rather than trying to build the eye-liner marking as geometry.

Now I'm working out the placement math: defining the head joint position at the end of the neck with its own forward direction, then positioning the skull sphere relative to that joint with an asymmetric scale, and figuring out the decal's anchor point and facing direction so the eyes sit correctly on the sides of the head.

For the beak, I'm considering whether to use a simple spike cone or a curved bezier sweep for a more natural shape, checking how the local-point and frame helper functions behave so I can anchor the beak geometry correctly to the head bone.

Now I'm planning the lower beak with its own jaw joint attached under the head, sweeping a slightly shorter curved shape from jaw to tip, and thinking through beak coloring options like a gold-to-pale-yellow gradient before moving on to designing the crest plumes on the crown.

Side plumes spread outward with gold-to-red gradient colors, built via a reusable ribbon-plume helper that orients flat sideways so the crest curves like feathers. I'm also planning cheek tufts, throat details, and the long neck geometry.

Now thinking through body shading: a countershaded palette with crimson back, orange flanks, and golden-cream chest, possibly mottled, with cards layered over top to hide the base pattern.

For the card texture itself, I'm scattering flame-shaped feather cards across the body and neck surfaces, using two gold-orange-red color variants for variety, with the cards leaning and bending to flow backward. Writing SVG path code...

I'm now thinking about wing coverts on the arms, deciding between card scatter versus layered feather extrusions. To keep part count manageable, I'll add one row of extruded greater coverts plus scattered cards on top for fluff, rather than building out multiple full rows.

Running the numbers, I estimate roughly 112 feathers across both wings plus the tail ribbons, which stays comfortably under budget, and triangle counts with feathers and cards together land around 7k, still fine. For Genshin-style gold ornamentation, I'm planning a gold collar band looping around the neck base, swept as a thin ring, with a gem accent to follow.

Now I'm layering on more jewelry: gold anklets swept around the legs, gold wrist bracers at the arm joints, a small gold tiara with a red gem on the forehead, and a chest pendant with a ruby or teal gemstone for that Genshin flavor. I'm also thinking about dark crimson flame-edge tips on the primary feathers and settling on a gold/orange palette with pale gold, standard gold, and orange tones.

I'm defining a gradient flame tail going from gold at the root through orange to red to crimson, and planning the wing arm as a tapering tube with a dark red leading edge. I'm importing the builder utilities I need, being careful to only pull in what's actually used so the typecheck doesn't flag unused imports.

Setting up the color palette and joint hierarchy, starting with a root "hips" joint tagged as spine, then building out the spine as a catmull-rom curve through a series of 3D points rising upward and forward.

Still defining skeleton chains...

Tuning the body radius profile with a sine-based taper so it thickens in the middle and narrows at the ends, then moving on to shape the neck sweep.

For the neck I'm narrowing its radius progressively from base to head, applying a gold/orange countershaded gradient. Then I'm attaching a head joint off the final neck point, using the neck's tangent frame at t=1 to set its position and orientation.

Now I'm positioning the skull as a slightly squashed sphere offset forward from the head joint, scaled to be a bit longer front-to-back, and leaning toward a plain warm gold color for simplicity before moving on to eye decals.

I'm sketching an anime-style eye texture as an SVG with a heavy dark lid shape, a pale iris ellipse, and plan to add pupil and highlight layers, though I'm still refining the exact curves and colors.

Working through the viewer's orientation, I determine the bird's front faces the viewer's left, so the eye decal's inner corner should sit toward the left (beak side) with the outer corner raised slightly higher, flowing back toward the tail.

For the mirroring logic, I conclude the side decal needs `mirror: s < 0` since the left flank (s=1) reads as drawn while the right flank (s=-1) needs flipping to keep the front-facing orientation consistent. Positioning the eyes' facing direction and anchor point relative to the head joint using the side sign s.

Now I'm sketching out a ribbon helper function for building crest/plumes, taking a path of points, max width, thickness, colors, bone, and name, planning to represent the points as plain arrays rather than Vector3 objects for simplicity.

Still writing ribbon sweep logic...

I'm thinking through how the path frame's roll orientation affects ribbon width direction as the tail bone curves from horizontal to vertical — the binormal stays roughly horizontal, which should work fine for the trailing flame effect. Now I'm planning the crest plumes as five ribbons radiating from the crown: a center one, two mid ones, and two outer ones.

Each plume's path is built from head-relative offset points with x-spread scaled by index, curving backward and downward with increasing droop and width toward the tips, plus some waviness. I'm also considering adding a couple of long whisker-like streamer cards from the cheek area to complement the crest.

Checking whether the cheek streamers would clip through the neck or wing geometry given their arc trajectory, I'm adjusting the endpoint coordinates to keep them clear of the shoulder/wing region.

Cheek streamers risk overlapping wing feathers along the back trajectory, so I decide to drop them and rely on the crest alone for ornamentation. Instead I'm planning a small gold tiara at the forehead with a red gem accent, plus a gold circlet loop sweeping around the skull.

Still refining tiara construction...

Now for the wings, I'm defining a helper function to build each wing symmetrically, placing shoulder, elbow, wrist, and wingtip joints mirrored by side, and chaining them off the nearest spine joint as parent using a polyline path.

I'm working out that four named joints create three bone spans, then mapping flight feather groups to their anatomical spans: primaries attached near the wrist-to-tip bone, secondaries along the elbow-to-wrist span, and tertials closer to the shoulder.

For smooth wing contours I'm using Catmull-Rom interpolation across the shoulder/elbow/wrist/tip points instead of a sharp polyline, and sweeping a tapering tube along the arm with a reddish gradient to represent the limb before feathers are layered on.

I'm defining a feather-generation function that takes a base position, direction, length, width, and bone reference, computing a perpendicular vector by crossing the up axis with the direction to establish the feather's outline plane...

I need to fix the handedness of this perpendicular vector so it consistently points toward the trailing edge for both the left and right wing, since mirroring the direction flips the cross product sign and would otherwise make the leading/trailing edges swap sides.

Now I'm sketching the outline function signature for the feather shape, and deciding whether to rely on an exported OutlinePoint type from the builder package or just define the return type locally to avoid import risk.

Defining the outline point coordinates...

Mapping out the flame tip coordinates...

Now I'm setting up the feather extrusion call with position, direction, width vectors, thickness, and smoothing parameters, confirming the types work with plain number arrays as points/directions. For color, I'm planning a gradient along the feather's length—gold at the root transitioning through orange to a crimson tip—and considering adding a thin bright shaft rod running along the feather's spine.

I'll add shaft rods only to primaries and secondaries (~34 feathers), using a deep orange color, positioned slightly above the feather plane to avoid z-fighting. To prevent adjacent feathers from overlapping in the same plane, I'll stagger each feather's vertical lift incrementally, with coverts placed higher still.

Now I'm working out the actual placement for the nine primary feathers per wing: computing each one's base position along the wrist-to-hand-tip line, its outward angle sweeping from about 55° down to -5° across the series, its rise, and its length using a sine-based variation so the primaries fan out naturally.

I'm finding the lengths peak somewhere in the middle feathers and taper at the tip and base, giving a total wingspan around 4.2-4.7 meters -- quite large compared to the body scale, but fitting for a dramatic phoenix-style wing, so I'm scaling the lengths down slightly to rein in the span a bit.

Now I'm working out the feather widths and spacing so they overlap nicely along the wing, then defining the secondary feathers between the elbow and wrist, blending their angles and lengths smoothly into the primaries.

Still calculating feather geometry...

Covert bases align with the flight feather bases along the arm axis, so they cluster near that region rather than spreading across the whole wing, with slight lift offsets so they layer without clipping through the tube geometry. I'm considering giving the wings a slight dihedral angle for added depth when viewed from the front.

Adding a gentle upward curve to the primaries so the wingtips rise slightly higher than the base. I'm also setting up a gold wrist band looping around the arm joint, scattering small flame-shaped cards along the arm sweep for texture, and placing a trio of small alula feathers near the wrist pointing forward.

Now adding a small gold claw spike at the wrist, then moving to the tail structure: setting up a red tail stalk sweep tapering in radius, with nine ribbon feathers arranged symmetrically along the tail bone.

Still writing tail feather paths...

Adding tail layers...

Each tail feather gets a flame-like wave motion with randomized phase per ribbon. For body details, I'm adding a gold chest ornament—a ruby pendant positioned on the front of the chest using spherical coordinates, plus a small gold ring accent nearby.

Finally I'm adding talon spikes jutting from the tips of each toe at a downward angle, with a dark crimson-black color for contrast, and adjusting the hind toe's position to point backward.
